title: Uptime partnering — 90d ramp & experiment canvas
content:
Purpose:
This canvas is a lightweight, experiment-first 90-day plan to operationalize SLOs with feature teams. The goal is to create a repeatable ramp pattern that aligns signals, short experiments (probes), and a minimal rollout gating to improve service uptime and reduce false positives in incident detection.

Context / why now:
- Recent incidents showed noisy alerts and unclear ownership between product and infra teams.
- Several feature teams are ready to adopt an SLO + guardrail approach but need a concrete playbook and telemetry checklist.
- We want a low-friction pilot that proves measurable reliability uplift and a handoff kit for scaling.

Objective (90d):
- Run 3 fast experiments across 2 feature teams to validate signal alignment and a single error-budget-driven rollout pattern.
- Reduce alert-to-action time by 30% for pilot services and cut false-positive pager noise by 25%.
- Produce a handoff kit (runbook template, telemetry checklist, alerting thresholds) for org-wide adoption.

Success metrics (primary):
- SLO adherence improvement: baseline -> +5–10% availability within 90d for pilot services.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) reduced by 30%.
- Alert fatigue reduction: >25% fewer redundant alerts during business hours.
- Ready-for-scale artifacts: 1 runbook template, 1 telemetry checklist, 1 rollout gating doc.

Stakeholders & roles (RACI - textual):
- Responsible: Feature Team Lead (instrumentation), SRE Partner (experiment design + runbook), Observability Engineer (query + dashboards).
- Accountable: Service Owner (release decision), Eng SRE Manager (program cadence).
- Consulted: Product Manager (user impact), Solutions Eng (customer-facing communications).
- Informed: Support & Oncall rotation.

90-day cadence (weekly/biweekly):
- Week 0 (kickoff): scoping + signal inventory; baseline collection for 7 days.
- Weeks 1–3: experiment sprint 1 (probe): adjust alert thresholds, add dedupe rules, enable a prefix KV cache experiment where applicable. Quick retros.
- Weeks 4–6: experiment sprint 2: rollout of lightweight client-side retries + backoff probes and measure error budget consumption.
- Weeks 7–9: experiment sprint 3: canary SLO gating for a small percentage of traffic + runbook dry-run.
- Weeks 10–12: consolidation, documentation, and handoff; measurement and exec summary.

Experiment backlog (examples, prioritized):
1) Alert dedupe & signal reconciliation (Pilot A) — reduce duplicate notifications by tuning grouping and severity.
2) Prefix/KV cache health probe (Pilot B) — measure hit-rate impact on tail latency and error surface.
3) Canary SLO gating (Pilot A) — route 2% traffic through fallback model variant if error budget nearing threshold.
4) Latency budget recharacterization (Pilot B) — split p50/p95 targets and validate user impact.

Telemetry & dashboard checklist (minimum viable):
- SLO time-window and objective configured in the SLO store (objective value, golden metrics).
- Error budget burn rate chart (1m, 15m, 1h windows).
- Alert-to-ack timeline (MTTA) and paging frequency by alert rule.
- Top contributing errors (tagged by root-cause labels).
- Canary traffic split and fallback activation rate.
- Simple playbook link on the dashboard.

Rollout gating and rollback triggers (conservative):
- Gate to proceed from canary -> full if: 14-day rolling SLO compliance >= objective and error budget burn rate < 0.5x baseline.
- Immediate rollback if: error budget burns > 3x baseline for 30 minutes, or user-facing errors spike > 2x baseline (p95 failure rate).

Communication plan (templates):
- Pre-kickoff: brief to stakeholders (1 pager + required telemetry).
- Experiment start: Slack channel + weekly summary.
- Incident during experiment: follow standard incident comms + tag experiment lead.
- Post-experiment: send one-slide summary to reliability-metrics and product leads.

Artifacts to produce by day 90:
- Runbook template: ownership, triggers, play actions, rollback steps, postmortem checklist.
- Telemetry checklist: queries, dashboards, SLO config example.
- Experiment journal: notes, metrics snapshots, decisions, and RFC for scaling.

Meeting rhythm (suggested):
- Weekly 30m experiment sync (SRE + feature team) — blockers and quick decisions.
- Biweekly 60m review (program leads + PMs) — status, escalations, decisions.
- End-of-sprint demo + retrospective (30–45m).

Quick operational checklists (for feature teams):
- Before experiment: confirm instrumentation present, baseline data collected for >= 7 days, create dashboard.
- During experiment: log any manual mitigations, annotate dashboard with experiment start times, maintain Slack channel.
- After experiment: capture lessons, update runbook, mark decisions in Confluence.

Notes to self / open questions:
- How to standardize SLO windows across stateful vs stateless services? (short term: align on 1h rolling + 7d reporting; iterate).
- Decide whether to centralize alert aggregation in platform or let teams tune rules locally.
- Evaluate cost tradeoffs for longer-term telemetry retention for experiment archives.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: experiments add noise during peak. Mitigation: small traffic canaries and rollback rules.
- Risk: teams lack instrumentation. Mitigation: quick instrumentation sprint (2 days) prioritized before experiment.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Book kickoff with Pilot A and Pilot B leads (target week 0).
2) Create baseline dashboards and SLO entries in the SLO registry; obs eng to provision queries.
3) Draft runbook template and share for feedback.
4) Open experiment tickets: JIRA-OPS-842 (Pilot A) and JIRA-OPS-843 (Pilot B).

Contact / owner notes:
- Owner: Maya Chen (eng-sre).
- Primary SRE partner for Pilot A: Jordan Lee.
- Primary SRE partner for Pilot B: Priya Nair.

--END--
